title: chronological-sse-emitter-and-escape-delimiter-reconciler
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: sporadic partial-JSON emits and out-of-order toolcall sentinel delivery were observed under high concurrency and aggressive batching. This caused downstream OpenAI-compat clients and structured-output parsers to drop events or mis-associate function calls. This PR introduces a chronological emitter watermark and an escape-delimiter reconciler to guarantee ordered emission of SSE events and preserve JSON token boundaries across chunk reassembly. Key changes: 1) emitter watermarking: each stream attaches a monotonically increasing emission watermark and a small in-flight ledger enabling deterministic stitch ordering at flush time; 2) escape-delimiter reconciler: rewrites delimiter coalescing such that trailing escape bytes are never left dangling across chunk boundaries and introduces a conservative fallback that injects a zero-width marker when reassembly ambiguity is detected; 3) fncall handoff stabilization: preserves fncall sentinel ordinal by delaying toolcall emit until its full JSON payload is confirmed by the watermark; 4) compatibility adapter: OpenAI-compat layer now tolerates the new zero-width marker and translates it back to canonical sentinel when delivering to legacy clients; 5) observability hooks: added sse.emitter.watermark_lag and sse.emitter.reconcile_count metrics and a debug trace to follow reassembly decisions. Testing: added deterministic unit tests that fuzz chunk splits, integration e2e that simulates interleaved KV-cache hits and batching, and a compatibility harness exercising toolcall interleavings against openai-compatible SDK. Rollout: feature guarded under flag runtime.sse.reconciler_enabled; default on for canary and off for global until 1 week of canary telemetry. Migration and safety: introduces no protocol breaking change for compliant clients; legacy adapters treat the marker as a no-op. See linked Linear items for follow-ups. review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can you clarify why we chose a zero-width marker vs escaping the delimiter? Aisha: Zero-width marker is a minimal surface change that is ignored by compliant JSON parsers and avoids double-escaping busy paths, we map it in the adapter for legacy clients.

Priya Sundaram: The watermark ledger might increase mem pressure under pathological queues; any heuristics? Aisha: added a cap and TTL on ledger entries and a circuit-breaker that forces immediate reconcile under memory pressure; documented in code comments.
Mateo Ruiz: Add perf numbers. Aisha: added canary telemetry baseline and observed median latency increase <= 1.2% at high qps, reconcile_count correlated with extreme split patterns only.

release_notes: Fixes rare SSE partial-JSON and toolcall ordering issues under heavy concurrent batching by introducing an emitter watermark and delimiter reconciler. Adds a conservative marker for ambiguous reassembly and updates the OpenAI compatibility adapter to transparently translate the marker for legacy clients. Flagged rollout and observability added.
